reason: It's free and runs locally, and I'm merging agent-written PRs I don't fully read, so I'd clone it and try it once on a side project. Whether it stays installed depends on the first run, not the pitch.
objection: Recording scenarios sounds like more work than writing tests, and a diff of every field that changed will probably flag timestamps and IDs and bury me in noise. I also don't know what running Meta's models locally costs me in setup and GPU.
would_change_my_mind: A README demo where it catches a real regression an AI agent introduced that our existing tests missed, set up in under 10 minutes with no noisy diffs.
